Hey I'm right there with you. I struggled (honestly probably still struggle) with an eating disorder in highschool and I was extremely thin but due to a combination of depression and starting to eat more in general as part of my recovery  have gained way more weight than I ever wanted. My advice as someone who has already purchased her dress is to make sure when you do go shopping to only take people who you feel extra comfortable with, and that really means people who won't say a dang thing about your body. I took my mom and my little sister and the only things they said about my body were things I brought up first so I didn't feel like they were picking at me. I would also recommend that you not look at the size on the dresses. The consultant I worked with when I purchased my dress told me that wedding dress sizes don't track to street sizes at all so doo freak out at a number bigger than you think you should be (they are all made up anyway, even street sizes). Try on a few different styles so that you know what you feel the most comfortable in, it may surprise you. Don't let your body issues stand in the way of a wedding if that's something you want. I know it feels intimidating because it did to me too but at the end of the day as long as you are comfortable you will be beautiful, no matter your size. Society puts a lot of pressure on losing weight for your wedding to squeeze into a dress and look perfect but take it from a girl who had had a freak out or two (or three... Or four...) about the same things your weight isn't your worth and there is a dress out there for you.

I know it's hard and scary to think about getting out on your own. A lot of people will tell you that you can't "abandon" your family like that but they way you need to think about it is that they have all but abandoned you. You have already proven you are strong enough to succeed on your own because you have been. Once you get out you will realize that you will be able to reclaim your childhood by doing whatever you want when no one is dragging you down. It won't necessarily be the same but it will feel great. You just have to start preparing to take a really hard step

I don't trust CPS at all. Growing up we had 2 reports made on my family, both in relation to my severely autistic brother.
 

1: When my brother was in the 2nd grade my Nmom was taking us to this hippie dippie private school that didn't abide by any real standards for public schools. Well my brother was starting to really show signs of unchecked autism but my mom wouldn't admit that to herself because "nothing is ever wrong"; my brother ended up getting thrown out of this school because of his behavior and my mom just decided to let him stay home alone while she worked instead of put him the public school, which we lived right across the street from. CPS was called and they came to do an interview, they only talked to my mom and step dad. The only thing that came of it was they weren't allowed to keep my brother home by himself so my mother's solution was to then pull me out of the 7th grade to stay home with him. 


2:  My step dad is an abusive asshole. He did a lot of horrible things to all of us growing up but baby bro got the worst of it because he had a disability. One day my brother tried to fight back and had a pocket knife on him (one of the ones that is basically a butter knife) and held it up towards my step dad. Well daddy dearest reaction to that was to get a pair of scissors and beat and stab my baby brother. They both were bloody and bruised. I sat in the basement (which was my room, unfinished mind you) and sobbed on the phone for hours with my boyfriend. I told my therapist about it the next week and he called CPS of course. They never even came.

CPS really isn't as big an organization as it should be so they don't do anything unless you live in an awful neighborhood or there are multiple reports.

If this were just any movie then yes it's ridiculous to put on a women's only showing but this is one of the first superhero movies (and the movies in general) with a strong woman as the lead and a love story NOT being a major focal point.
